title: Candle confession
idea: an old man at a candlelit table says one sentence to someone off-screen
style: period drama, Rembrandt lighting, warm low-key, fine grain
subject: an old man with a white beard and a lined face, wearing a dark wool coat, hands folded on the table
setting: a farmhouse kitchen at night, a single candle on a wooden table, the rest of the room in shadow
light: candlelight as the only source, warm flicker, Rembrandt triangle on the far cheek, rapid falloff into darkness

beats.action: he stares at the candle, the flame reflected in his eyes, breathing slowly
he looks up at someone off-screen to the right
he says the line, slowly, and his hands tighten
beats.camera: continue the push-in to a close-up

beats.action: he looks back down at the flame; it flickers

physics: the flame flickers and the light on his face flickers with it; natural micro-movements, breathing, a slow blink; hands tighten with visible tendons

sound.ambience: quiet room, wind outside, a clock ticking
sound.dialogue: The old man says, slowly, lip-synced: "I never told her it was me."

notes: 'flicker' in the negative list refers to exposure flicker; the candle flicker is described in the light and physics fields, which models separate well.
